প্রজ্ঞাপন

তারিখ, ১৭ আষাঢ়, ১৪২২ বঙ্গাব্দ/১ জুলাই, ২০১৫ খ্রিস্টাব্দ

এস, আর, ও নং ২০৭-আইন/২০১৫/৪৪/কাস্টমস।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969), অতঃপর উক্ত Act বলিয়া উল্লিখিত, এর section 202A এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে সরকার, অনাদায়যোগ্য সরকারি পাওনা অবলোপনের (Write off) লক্ষ্যে নিম্নরূপ বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করিল, যথা:-

Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal authority under section 202A for the government to frame rules regarding the write-off of unrecoverable government dues.
It is referred to as the principal statute governing the issuance of these regulatory orders.
Write-off of Unrecoverable Government Du: The government has established specific rules to govern the process of writing off government dues that are deemed unrecoverable.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১। সংক্ষিপ্ত শিরোনাম।- এই বিধিমালা সরকারি পাওনা অবলোপন বিধিমালা, ২০১৫ নামে অভিহিত হইবে।

Government Dues Write-off Rules 2015: This clause formally establishes the title of the regulations as the Government Dues Write-off Rules 2015.

Customs Act 1969: This act is the primary legislation governing customs activities in Bangladesh and is the law referred to as 'the Act' in this context.
Bankruptcy: The term is defined by reference to the specific debtor definition provided under the relevant national bankruptcy legislation.
Person: The term encompasses various legal structures including companies, partnership firms, associations, and other bodies of individuals.
National Board of Revenue: This entity is defined as the authority constituted under the National Board of Revenue Order 1972.
Customs Duty: Customs and other taxes are defined to include those applicable under the Customs Act 1969, the repealed Sales Tax Ordinance 1984, and the Value Added Tax Act 1991.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: This act serves as one of the legal bases for the collection and determination of applicable taxes.
Government Revenue Collection: Government revenue or dues refer specifically to the outstanding amounts described under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৩। অবলোপনযোগ্য সরকারি পাওনা।- যেই ক্ষেত্রে বিদ্যমান আইন অথবা তদধীন প্রণীত বিধিমালার অধীন কোন শুল্ক ও কর বা অন্য কোন অর্থ কোন ব্যক্তি কর্তৃক সরকারের নিকট প্রদেয় হয় অথবা কোন ব্যক্তির বিরুদ্ধে কোন অর্থদণ্ড আরোপ করা হয় এবং উক্ত শুল্ক, অর্থদণ্ড অথবা অন্যান্য অর্থ নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে পরিশোধ করা হয় নাই এবং উক্ত ব্যক্তির দেউলিয়াত্বের (bankruptcy) অথবা নিখোঁজ (Untraceable) হওয়ার অথবা অন্য কোন কারণে উক্ত শুল্ক, অর্থদণ্ড বা অর্থ বিদ্যমান আইনে ব্যবস্থিত পদ্ধতিতে তাহার নিকট হইতে আদায় করা যায় নাই অথবা আদায়যোগ্য নয় সেই ক্ষেত্রে বিধি ৪ এ উল্লিখিত পদ্ধতিতে উহা অবলোপন করা যাইবে।

Customs Duty and Taxes: These are government dues or penalties payable by a person under existing laws or rules that remain unpaid after the specified period.
When such amounts are deemed unrecoverable due to bankruptcy, the person being untraceable, or other legal impediments, they may be written off following the procedure prescribed in the rules.
Bankruptcy: This is identified as a legal condition under which outstanding government dues, duties, or penalties may be considered for write-off if they cannot be recovered through standard legal processes.

Government Revenue Write-off: This clause establishes the procedural mechanism for writing off uncollectible government revenue.

The process requires the submission of data by the Commissioner of Customs to the National Board of Revenue, presentation at a board meeting, and final approval by the government before an order is issued to formally write off the dues.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is responsible for reporting uncollectible government revenue to the National Board of Revenue using a specified form as defined in the relevant appendix.
National Board of Revenue: The Board acts as the central administrative body in the write-off process by receiving information from the Commissioner, reviewing it in a formal meeting, seeking government approval, and issuing the final order for the write-off.

Irrecoverable Government Dues Write-off: This form specifies the information required to process the write-off of government dues that cannot be collected from importers or exporters.
The form requires documentation on the importer or exporter's identification, the context of the dues, recovery attempts made, and a detailed breakdown of the taxes, penalties, and interest involved.
Value Added Tax: The form requires the submission of Value Added Tax registration details for individuals or entities with outstanding dues.
Customs Duty: The form mandates an assessment of whether the person with outstanding dues possesses any goods that are subject to customs duty and are available for sale.
